title: Cross-team engineering leadership weekly staff notes — 2026-03-09
content:
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (chair), Diego Martinez, Priya Nair, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Alvarez, Chen Wei, plus notes from SRE (J. Patel) and Product (R. Gomez)
Apologies: Nina Brooks (on leave)
Meeting length: 45m

Purpose: weekly cross-team sync to surface risks, coordinate rollouts, and unblock cross-cutting infra/workstreams. Focus this week: rollout cadence for kernel-selection changes, Dedicated capacity capacity planning for Q2, and SLO incidents review.

Agenda:
1) Quick round-robin team updates (5m each)
2) Kernel selection rollout status and canary results (10m)
3) Dedicated capacity / Q2 pool sizing (10m)
4) Recent SLO breaches and mitigation plan (10m)
5) Action items and next steps (5m)

Notes by agenda item:
1) Team updates (high level)
- Serving-runtime (Diego): kernel-selection rollout currently in canary v2 on 10% of traffic. Early metrics show 6–8% cost reduction for long-seq workloads but p95 latency increased by ~10ms on narrow cases. We suspect a scheduling edge-case with short sequences + small batch sizes. Investigating.
- Private-deployments (Priya): one on-prem pilot deployed to customer X; onboarding docs updated. Hit a key issue with KMS integration (timeout under cold-start) — workaround applied (increase KMS client timeout) and follow-up ticket created.
- Console & Observability (Sofia): new per-route token cost dashboard landed in staging. Need a small change to attribution logic (edge-case when requests fallback to model-variant).
- SRE (Chen Wei / J. Patel): saw two small SLO breaches last week (p50 OK, p95 spikes during 2026-03-05 11:00–12:30 UTC). Root cause: burst of concurrent long-context streaming requests + autoscaler cooldown misconfiguration. Mitigated by rolling restart + temporary autoscaler param adjustments.
- Product (R. Gomez, brief): prioritizing rollout of model-version pinning in Hosted API next sprint to support customer Y's compliance request.

2) Kernel selection rollout and canary results
- Summary: Canary v2 uses new kernel selector that prefers quantized kernels for encoder-heavy blocks; shows cost improvements on synthetic long-context benchmarks.
- Findings: 6–8% token cost reduction for >2k token sequences; however p95 regression on short sequences (<=128 tokens) in some TPU-backed hosts. Hypothesis: kernel switch causes increased memcpy overhead for small batches.
- Discussion: decision to pause expanding canary to 30% until the memcpy overhead is addressed. Diego to add microbenchmark that reproduces short-seq regression on affected infra.
- Temporary mitigation: route short-seq traffic to v1 kernel path by request classifier (implemented as routing rule in the control plane). Priya to review rule for Private deployments to ensure parity.

3) Dedicated capacity / Q2 pool sizing
- Finance ask: provide committed GPU pool sizing by 2026-03-20 for Q2 forecasting.
- Usage snapshot: last 30d average utilization for Dedicated pools = 68%; burst tail (95th) = 93% during marketing spike.
- Proposal: increase base reserved pool by 12% and add 20% burstable capacity for marketing-heavy regions (us-west, eu-west).
- Risks: cost impact vs. potential lost revenue from throttled customers. Action: Liam to prepare a sensitivity model (cost vs. SLA/throughput impact) due 2026-03-16.

4) SLO incidents and mitigation
- Incident summary (2026-03-05): p95 latency spike related to autoscaler cooldown + sudden long-context streaming increase.
- Immediate fixes applied: lowered cooldown window for scale-up, increased max concurrency per instance for streaming endpoints, and applied temporary routing to less-loaded regions.
- Next steps: implement request-aware autoscaling signal that factors in active KV-cache size (priority). Engineering estimate: 3 sprints. Priya and SRE to define signals and acceptance criteria.

5) Action items (owner — due)
- Diego: add microbench reproducer for short-seq memcpy regression and open a detailed perf ticket with profiling traces — due 2026-03-12.
- Priya: verify control-plane routing rule parity for Private deployments and document in runbook — due 2026-03-11.
- Liam: produce Dedicated capacity sensitivity model (cost vs. SLA impact) and share with Finance & Sales — due 2026-03-16.
- Sofia: fix attribution logic in per-route cost dashboard and push to staging; include test cases for model-variant fallback — due 2026-03-13.
- Chen Wei (SRE): draft request-aware autoscaler signals and a high-level implementation plan for review — due 2026-03-23.
- Alyssa: schedule cross-team deep-dive on kernel selector with infra partners; target 60m session next week (invite to be sent) — due 2026-03-10.

Decisions made:
- Pause canary expansion to 30% until short-seq regression is understood and mitigated.
- Route short-seq traffic to v1 kernel path as a temporary mitigation.
- Proceed with preliminary Dedicated pool bump plan (12% base, 20% burst) pending Liam's sensitivity analysis.

Open questions / risks:
- Will the memcpy overhead be addressable in the v2 selector, or will we need a hybrid path permanently?
- Private deployments: does the KMS timeout workaround have long-term implications for compliance or auditability? (Priya to consult security).
- Autoscaler: can we define robust cache-aware signals without adding excessive noise that causes flapping?

Metrics snapshot (quick):
- Token throughput (global avg, last 24h): 1.2B tokens/day
- p95 latency (text generation, hosted): 310ms (baseline target 280ms)
- Error rate (5xx) last 7d: 0.12%
- Dedicated pool avg utilization (30d): 68%

Links / references (in-meeting):
- Kernel selector PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412
- Canary metrics dashboard (internal): slack link posted in #infra-canaries
- Incident timeline: JIRA-INFRA-987
- On-prem KMS issue ticket: JIRA-SEC-2101

Notes-to-self / rough TODOs (informal):
- Follow up with Product on customer Y compliance timeline — might accelerate hosted pinning work.
- Consider an automated canary rollback if p95 > 10% over baseline for any 12h window.
- Remind Solutions Eng to run the Dedicated pooling playbook before the next major marketing event.

Next meeting: 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC
